provenance.note: Two rows of retired history tables that the frozen codec rejects. Each of the thirteen retired history tables is one conversion unit, so before RFC-626 one such row withheld the whole package of its table and the new daemon could not build its history query index. A code finding whose integer column holds text cannot be read back from a package, so it is set aside on its own and the package holds the other rows; only SQLite can hold it (the old PostgreSQL column is typed). A round stage whose JSON column holds text that does not parse still has its column's type, so it goes into the package as read and the decision is recorded.

rows.why: §9.9 row 8: text in an integer column does not read back from a package; the row is set aside on its own
§3.4 row 8 / §9.9: JSON text that does not parse keeps its column's type and goes into the package as read
